title: LD pruning

blocks.what_we_do: We select a smaller set of [autosomal](../docs/glossary.md#autosome) variants that are less correlated with each other. Autosomes are the chromosomes 1 to 22. We use this set for the heterozygosity check, for the relatedness check and, later, for [PCA](../docs/glossary.md#pca-pc). PCA (principal component analysis) is a method that summarises the genetic differences between people.
blocks.why:
[Linkage disequilibrium](../docs/glossary.md#ld) (LD) means that alleles at nearby sites are correlated. A dense region with many correlated sites would count too much, only because the array has many [probes](../docs/glossary.md#probe) there. A probe is the piece of DNA on the array that measures one site.

[LD pruning](../docs/glossary.md#ld-pruning) keeps one representative subset of sites. It does not delete the other sites from the association data.

We also leave out the long-range LD regions, where the correlation reaches over very long distances. The GRCh38 intervals are listed in the helper function. They are not a complete catalogue for all studies.
blocks.command:
```{r s3-4}
regions <- guided_high_ld(cfg)
run_plink(cfg, c("--pfile", guided_path(cfg, "3.3"), "--chr", "1-22", "--maf", "0.05", "--geno", "0.02",
  "--exclude", "bed1", regions, "--indep-pairwise", "200kb", "0.2", "--out", guided_path(cfg, "3.4", "prune")))
pruned <- readLines(paste0(guided_path(cfg, "3.4", "prune"), ".prune.in"))
stopifnot(length(pruned) == 69539L)
cat(length(pruned), "variants kept by LD pruning\n")
guided_artifact_checkpoint(cfg, "3.4", c(paste0(guided_path(cfg, "3.4", "prune"), c(".prune.in", ".prune.out")), regions), parent = "3.3")
```

Plain PLINK 2 command (use `bin\plink2.exe` on Windows):

```sh
bin/plink2 --pfile results/guided/s3-3_state --chr 1-22 --maf 0.05 --geno 0.02 --exclude bed1 results/guided/s3-4_high_ld.bed1 --indep-pairwise 200kb 0.2 --out results/guided/s3-4_prune --threads 2 --memory 2048
```

`--chr 1-22` keeps only the autosomes. `--maf 0.05` keeps common variants, which means a [minor allele frequency](../docs/glossary.md#maf) (MAF) of at least 5%. `--geno 0.02` removes variants with more than 2% missing genotypes, so this subset has a variant call rate of at least 98%. `--exclude bed1` leaves out the sites inside the listed regions. The file gives them as one-based inclusive intervals (positions counted from 1, with both ends included). `--indep-pairwise 200kb 0.2` prunes within windows of 200 kb (200,000 base pairs of DNA), with a limit of 0.2 for the squared correlation, called [r^2](../docs/glossary.md#r-squared). `--out`, `--threads` and `--memory` have the meanings given at step 3.1.
blocks.expected_result:
The `.prune.in` file lists 69,539 sites. The complete analysis state still has 296,360 variants.

The tested PLINK version is defined in `config.R` and recorded in
`software_versions.txt`. Validation: executable chunks and the expected counts passed on Windows. Your numbers should be the same.
blocks.troubleshooting: Stop at the first error. Check the input file named in the message and the previous step. Keep the command and the console messages. Do not use files from a different version of the dataset. See [troubleshooting](../docs/troubleshooting.md).
blocks.what_this_check_can_reveal: Regions that would otherwise dominate summaries made from correlated markers. The subset that you keep depends on the input samples and on the exact version of the algorithm.
blocks.quick_check:
Should the later association scan test only the pruned sites?

<details><summary>Show the answer</summary>

No. We use pruning only for specific checks and for the PCA. The association scan uses the full set of variants that pass QC.

</details>

setup_code:
start_dir <- setwd(if (file.exists("config.R")) "." else "..")
if (requireNamespace("knitr", quietly = TRUE)) knitr::opts_knit$set(root.dir = getwd())
source("R/guided.R")
cfg <- guided_init()
setwd(start_dir)

options.name: --exclude
options.explanation_markdown: `--exclude bed1` leaves out the sites inside the listed regions.

options.name: --geno
options.explanation_markdown: `--geno 0.02` removes variants with more than 2% missing genotypes, so this subset has a variant call rate of at least 98%.

options.name: --indep-pairwise
options.explanation_markdown: `--indep-pairwise 200kb 0.2` prunes within windows of 200 kb (200,000 base pairs of DNA), with a limit of 0.2 for the squared correlation, called [r^2](../docs/glossary.md#r-squared).

options.name: --maf
options.explanation_markdown: `--maf 0.05` keeps common variants, which means a [minor allele frequency](../docs/glossary.md#maf) (MAF) of at least 5%.

options.name: --memory
options.explanation_markdown: `--memory 2048` sets the memory limit to 2048 MiB (about 2 gigabytes).

options.name: --out
options.explanation_markdown: `--out` sets the name prefix of the output files.

options.name: --pfile
options.explanation_markdown: `--pfile` selects the input fileset in the PLINK 2 native format.

options.name: --threads
options.explanation_markdown: `--threads 2` limits the number of worker threads (parallel jobs).
